title: EXP-014 — Form Variable Definition Recovery Across Ordinary Designer Close/Reopen
objective: Using one new User-scope classic BuildFromScratch Form named FX_FormVariableLab04, establish all preconditions, create exactly one Form variable named FX_CloseReopenRetentionVar with Global=False, Persistent=True, and Value=Seed-Close-D, record every visible design-time definition field, perform exactly one ordinary Designer Save, verify the definition immediately after Save, then close the clean Form through the ordinary Designer Form-tab close control and reopen the same User-scoped Form through the supported recent-forms path. Compare every recorded visible variable-definition field after reopen to the saved baseline. This experiment tests only UI-level recovery of the design-time variable definition across that ordinary Form-tab close/reopen boundary.

in_scope: Before any Mongoose artifact mutation, establish or confirm a supported live Mongoose/Web Client session without exposing credential values.
Prove server-backed liveness, User editing scope, and that FX_FormVariableLab04 is absent exact and case-insensitively before mutation.
Create exactly one User-scope classic BuildFromScratch Form named FX_FormVariableLab04 using the verified basic-form recipe with Save Template unchecked.
Immediately after Form creation, while the Web Client session is live, prove exactly one case-insensitive FX_FormVariableLab04 exists in the live Select Form inventory.
Open Details > Variables and create exactly one Form variable named FX_CloseReopenRetentionVar.
Record every visible variable-definition field before Save.
Perform exactly one ordinary Designer Save and prove the Designer returns clean.
Immediately verify the variable definition still matches the pre-Save baseline.
Close FX_FormVariableLab04 once through its ordinary Designer Form-tab close control while clean.
Reopen FX_FormVariableLab04 once through the supported Designer Form-menu recent-forms path.
After reopen, prove Name, ScopeType, and ScopeName identify the intended User-scoped Form and compare every recorded visible variable-definition field against the saved baseline.
Capture screenshots and read-only diagnostics under evidence/EXP-014/ and update only the EXP-014 experiment record plus its evidence directory.
Prefer one bounded worker task for Form creation through post-reopen verification after preflight so session idle time does not become the tested variable.

Treating EXP-014 as a replay of EXP-013.
Testing runtime value initialization, mutation, retrieval, or runtime persistent-variable semantics.
Testing Persistent=False, Global=True, temporary variables, or a second comparison variable.
Testing explicit global-object unloading, metadata unloading, cache-clearing behavior, or preference-dependent cache behavior.
Testing logout/login, session replacement, browser restart, or a newly launched Designer client as the lifecycle boundary.
Testing any save path other than one ordinary Designer Save.
Testing Caption, Description, components, collections, bindings, validators, handlers, scripts, data sources, IDOs, localized Strings, portals, Runtime Builder, Responsive Form Builder, or FormSync.

acceptance_checks.description: Before any Mongoose artifact mutation, evidence proves a supported live session, a successful server-backed liveness check, User editing scope, and zero exact and zero case-insensitive live-inventory matches for FX_FormVariableLab04.

Exactly one new User-scope classic BuildFromScratch Form named FX_FormVariableLab04 is created through the verified basic-form recipe with Save Template unchecked, and immediately after creation live Select Form evidence proves exactly one case-insensitive target before variable mutation begins.

Before Save, Details > Variables visibly contains exactly one experiment-created variable named FX_CloseReopenRetentionVar with Global=False, Persistent=True, Value=Seed-Close-D where Value is exposed, and every visible variable-definition field is recorded as the comparison baseline.

Exactly one ordinary Designer Save occurs after variable creation; captured response or network evidence shows one successful save, no alternate or second save mechanism occurs, and the Designer returns to a demonstrably clean state.
Immediately after that Save and before closing the Form, exactly one FX_CloseReopenRetentionVar remains and every recorded visible design-time definition field equals the AC-3 baseline.
FX_FormVariableLab04 is closed exactly once using the ordinary Designer Form-tab close control while clean, with no unsaved-change prompt, and evidence proves the target Form is no longer open.

FX_FormVariableLab04 is deliberately reopened exactly once through the supported Designer Form-menu recent-forms path, and the loaded version is proven to be the intended User-scoped Form by Name, ScopeType, and ScopeName.
After reopen, Details > Variables contains exactly one FX_CloseReopenRetentionVar and every visible design-time definition field recorded in AC-3 equals the saved baseline; the Designer is clean.

Evidence and the experiment record prove that after FX_FormVariableLab04 creation began there was no login, Sign In/OK, deliberate reauthentication, logout, browser restart, deliberate session replacement, explicit metadata or cache operation, preferences action, runtime Form execution, alternate save path, or second Save.

The experiment record classifies only the observed UI-level recovery or non-recovery of the design-time variable definition across one ordinary Designer Form-tab close/reopen and explicitly makes no runtime-value, cache-eviction, database-durability, storage-provenance, or cross-session claim.

Final repository and worktree audit proves experiment-attributable changes are confined to the EXP-014 record and evidence/EXP-014/, with no recipe, AGENTS.md, environment, other experiment, existing FX_ artifact, or non-FX_ artifact modified.

notes: Proposed by the coordinator after run R-20261003-111321-knwH. Rationale: EXP-013 produced observed evidence that a Persistent=True, Global=False Form variable definition remained intact immediately across one ordinary Designer Save, but the run was non-accepted because its post-creation inventory requirement became impossible to prove after the Web Client session expired. The next experiment should not repair EXP-013. It should test the next distinct lifecycle boundary: whether the saved design-time variable definition is recovered after one ordinary Designer Form-tab close/reopen. The close/reopen path is already well characterized for Form Caption and Description metadata. To avoid repeating EXP-013's evidence-ordering problem, the exactly-one inventory state must be proven immediately after Form creation while the Web Client is live, before variable mutation.
